experiment_description: LaBi2 thin films were grown by molecular beam epitaxy on MgO (001) substrates using a two-step growth procedure and capped in situ with amorphous Ge. The films were stored in an N2 glovebox and measured within 24 hours of growth. Film thicknesses used for the parallel-field superconducting analysis were 2.1, 2.3, 2.7, 3.0, 8.5, 12, 23, 34, and 75 nm, as estimated from X-ray diffraction Laue fringes. Electronic transport was measured in a dilution refrigerator with base temperature about 20 mK and a two-axis vector magnet rated 9 T in one axis and 3 T in the other. A linear four-point geometry on rectangular samples measured longitudinal resistance using a lock-in amplifier with 100–500 nA bias current at 10–20 Hz. The magnetic field was aligned parallel to the film plane using an alignment procedure to obtain the in-plane upper critical field. The superconducting critical field curve H_parallel_c2(T) was determined from temperature-dependent resistance traces using the criterion R = 0.5 R0, where R0 is the normal-state resistance just above the transition. The measured H_parallel_c2(T) curves were fit to two dirty-limit pair-breaking models. In the Kharitonov-Feigel’man (KF) model, the fitted parameters were Tc0, the critical temperature in the absence of magnetic impurities; tau_s = 1/nu_s, the magnetic spin-exchange scattering time; tau_so, the spin-orbit scattering time; tau_tr, the transport scattering time entering the orbital depairing term; and sgn(J)zeta = sgn(J)nSJS/nu_s, the signed inverse Born parameter. The KF fitting assumed antiferromagnetic exchange coupling J > 0, impurity spin S = 5/2, pF estimated from normal-state Drude/free-electron analysis, nu_s and sgn(J)zeta varying by at most ±50% across the thickness series, and the lower-bound constraint tau_so/tau_tr >= 1. The Klemm-Luther-Beasley (KLB) model was fit using the dirty-limit expression with free parameters Tc,H=0 and tau_so; for films showing low-field deviations, the KLB fit was performed outside the low-field enhanced regime and extrapolated to zero field.

experiment_description: For the same MBE-grown, Ge-capped LaBi2 thickness series on MgO (001), in-plane upper critical fields were measured by four-point lock-in transport in a dilution refrigerator with a two-axis vector magnet. The magnetic field was aligned parallel to the film plane, and H_parallel_c2(T) was extracted using the R = 0.5 R0 criterion from superconducting transitions measured as a function of temperature and parallel magnetic field. To quantify violation of the weak-coupling BCS Pauli limit, the authors extrapolated H_parallel_c2 to T approaching 0 and compared it with H_P^BCS = 1.86 × Tc, where Tc is the zero-field critical temperature in kelvin used for the Pauli-limit estimate. Thickness dependence of the dimensionless ratio H_parallel_c2/H_P^BCS was analyzed over the measured film series using a power-law form H_parallel_c2/H_P^BCS proportional to t^alpha, where t is the LaBi2 film thickness and alpha is the fitted scaling exponent.

h_parallel_c2_over_bcs_pauli_limit_t_2p1.description: Approximate zero-temperature in-plane upper critical field divided by the conventional BCS Pauli limit for the 2.1 nm LaBi2 film, using the experimentally measured zero-field Tc for the Pauli-limit estimate.

pauli_limit_violation_thickness_scaling_.description: Fitted exponent alpha for the measured thickness dependence H_parallel_c2/H_P^BCS proportional to t^alpha.

experiment_description: Perpendicular-field superconducting upper critical fields were measured on the MBE-grown, Ge-capped LaBi2 films on MgO (001) using four-point electronic transport in the same dilution refrigerator and vector magnet setup. The applied magnetic field was oriented perpendicular to the film plane. For each film thickness in the series, H_perpendicular_c2(T) was extracted from the resistive superconducting transition as a function of temperature. The resulting H_perpendicular_c2(T) curves were fit to the single-gap Ginzburg-Landau form H_perpendicular_c2(T) = (Phi0/(2*pi*xi_ab^2))*(1 - (Tc/Tc,H=0)^2), where Phi0 is the superconducting flux quantum, xi_ab is the in-plane superconducting coherence length to be fitted, Tc is the temperature at which the critical field is evaluated, and Tc,H=0 is the zero-field critical temperature for that film.
